dimensions.label: Participants
dimensions.description: Who debates: persona design, functional roles, and base-model selection for each agent (node v in V).

subdimensions.label: Persona attributes
subdimensions.description: The three prompt-designed persona attribute families; each is a free-form field, not a mutually-exclusive choice.

values.label: Background
values.description: The identity, knowledge, and expertise of the agent.

values.label: Personality
values.description: Behavioural tendencies that shape how an agent debates.

values.label: Stance
values.description: A predefined positioning on the topic under discussion.

subdimensions.label: Persona heterogeneity
subdimensions.description: Whether debaters share one persona or are assigned distinct personas.

values.label: Homogeneous
values.description: All debaters share the same persona.

values.label: Heterogeneous
values.description: Debaters are assigned distinct personas.

subdimensions.label: Persona assignment
subdimensions.description: How personas are assigned to debaters.

values.label: Unspecified
values.description: No explicit persona is assigned.

values.label: Manually identified
values.description: Personas are assigned manually at design time.

values.label: Automatically identified
values.description: Personas are automatically assigned at runtime.

subdimensions.label: Roles
subdimensions.description: The functional roles an agent can take; a single participant may combine multiple roles.

values.label: Debater
values.description: Presents and defends positions, engaging in the exchange to reach consensus.

values.label: Judge
values.description: Delivers the final decision and may determine when consensus is reached.

values.label: Summarizer
values.description: Synthesizes debaters' statements to reduce token consumption.

values.label: Leader
values.description: Oversees and guides the debate (also called moderator).

values.label: Verifier
values.description: Fact-checks the statements produced by debaters.

values.label: Editor
values.description: Refines and produces the final response from the debate outcome.

subdimensions.label: Base model family
subdimensions.description: Whether the base model is proprietary or publicly available.

values.label: Closed-weight
values.description: Proprietary parameters, accessed via an external provider.

values.label: Open-weight
values.description: Publicly available parameters, deployable locally.

subdimensions.label: Base model heterogeneity
subdimensions.description: Whether all agents share one base model or draw on different ones.

values.label: Homogeneous
values.description: All agents share the same base model.

values.label: Heterogeneous
values.description: Agents draw on different base models.

dimensions.label: Interaction
dimensions.description: How agents communicate: topology (G=(V,E)), protocol (temporal edge activation E(t)), and message format (transformations m~=f(m)).

subdimensions.label: Topology adaptability
subdimensions.description: Whether communication channels change throughout the debate (E(t)).

values.label: Static
values.description: Communication channels remain unchanged throughout the debate.

values.label: Dynamic
values.description: Communication channels adapt throughout the debate.

subdimensions.label: Topology structure
subdimensions.description: The overall shape of the communication graph G=(V,E).

values.label: Fully connected
values.description: All agents interact with each other.

values.label: Divided into groups
values.description: Agents interact within disconnected subgroups.

values.label: Structured networks
values.description: Interaction follows a predefined network topology.

subdimensions.label: Topology pattern
subdimensions.description: Canonical structured-network patterns selectable when the structure is a structured network.

values.label: Chain
values.description: A linear topology where each agent builds on its predecessor.

values.label: Ring
values.description: A cyclic chain where each agent communicates with a fixed neighbour set.

values.label: Star
values.description: A centralized topology where a single node aggregates from all others.

values.label: Tree
values.description: A hierarchical topology enabling recursive decomposition of reasoning.

values.label: Layered network
values.description: A multi-stage topology where agents form sequential layers, each performing a distinct transformation.

values.label: Sparse
values.description: Each agent interacts with a limited subset of peers (|E| << |V|(|V|-1)).

values.label: Bipartite
values.description: Agents split into two disjoint sets interacting primarily across the partition.

subdimensions.label: Protocol mechanism
subdimensions.description: How agents take turns contributing to the debate.

values.label: Sequential
values.description: Agents intervene in ordered turns.

values.label: Simultaneous
values.description: Agents contribute to the debate at the same time.

values.label: Hybrid
values.description: Combines sequential and simultaneous exchanges.

subdimensions.label: Protocol ordering
subdimensions.description: How speaking order is determined for sequential turn-taking.

values.label: Fixed
values.description: A predefined speaking order.

values.label: Randomized
values.description: Randomized turn-taking to mitigate ordering/dominance bias.

values.label: Coordinator-selected
values.description: A coordinator/leader agent selects the next speaker from the evolving context.

subdimensions.label: Format syntax
subdimensions.description: The representation in which arguments are exchanged.

values.label: Natural language
values.description: Arguments are exchanged in human-readable text.

values.label: Embeddings
values.description: Arguments are exchanged as vector embeddings directly.

subdimensions.label: Format content
subdimensions.description: How argument content is transformed before being shared.

values.label: Verbatim
values.description: Full arguments are shared without modification.

values.label: Summarized
values.description: Arguments are compressed into shorter representations.

values.label: Other
values.description: Alternative content transformation strategies are applied.

subdimensions.label: Format content metadata
subdimensions.description: Optional signals attachable to an exchange, used to weight or guide aggregation.

values.label: Confidence
values.description: An agent's degree of certainty, used to weight aggregation.

values.label: Uncertainty
values.description: Typically the inverse of confidence.

values.label: Verifier score
values.description: A dedicated component scores answers and intermediate reasoning.

values.label: Judge likelihood
values.description: A judge assigns a plausibility signal used for final selection.

values.label: Bias/quality score
values.description: Auxiliary agents compute bias or quality scores to guide selection.

values.label: Guideline weight
values.description: External signals encoding priorities such as utility or fairness.

subdimensions.label: Format memory
subdimensions.description: The scope of context an agent can access.

values.label: Short-term
values.description: Access limited to current debate context.

values.label: Long-term
values.description: Access extends to persistent memory across debates.

values.label: Knowledge retrieval
values.description: Agents query external knowledge sources.

values.label: Parametric
values.description: Debates embedded into model parameters through training.

dimensions.label: Agreement
dimensions.description: How the debate resolves to a final output: the (authority, resolution) pair.

subdimensions.label: Authority
subdimensions.description: Who holds the power to make the final decision.

values.label: Collective
values.description: The final decision is made jointly by multiple agents.

values.label: Judge-based
values.description: The final decision is made by a designated judge agent.

values.label: Hybrid
values.description: The final decision combines collective and judge-based authority.

values.label: Other
values.description: User-dependent, undefined, or non-standard decision authority.

subdimensions.label: Resolution
subdimensions.description: The mechanism by which the debate resolves to a final output.

values.label: Majority vote
values.description: The option supported by most agents is selected.

values.label: Argument evaluation
values.description: The decision is made by evaluating the debate.

values.label: Weighted vote
values.description: Votes are aggregated with agent-specific weights.

values.label: Scoring
values.description: The decision is made through agent response scoring and ranking.

values.label: Average
values.description: The decision is derived by averaging agent outputs or scores.

values.label: Consensus
values.description: Agents deliberate until reaching a common agreement.

persona_patterns.label: Angel
persona_patterns.description: The optimistic, supportive advocate who argues the favourable position.

personas.name: Angel
personas.background: A constructive advocate who looks for merits and the strongest supporting case.
personas.personality: Optimistic, encouraging, and charitable in interpreting the proposal.
personas.stance: Argue in favour of the proposition and defend its strengths.

persona_patterns.label: Devil (devil's advocate)
persona_patterns.description: The adversarial critic who argues the opposing, sceptical position.

personas.name: Devil
personas.background: A sceptical critic trained to surface flaws, risks, and counter-arguments.
personas.personality: Adversarial, probing, and relentless in testing weak points.
personas.stance: Argue against the proposition and expose its weaknesses.

persona_patterns.label: Prosecution
persona_patterns.description: The accusing party in an adversarial legal-style debate.

personas.name: Prosecution
personas.background: A prosecutor building the case that the claim/charge holds.
personas.personality: Assertive, evidence-driven, and persuasive.
personas.stance: Argue that the claim is true / the charge is warranted.

persona_patterns.label: Defence
persona_patterns.description: The defending party in an adversarial legal-style debate.

personas.name: Defence
personas.background: A defender rebutting the case and raising reasonable doubt.
personas.personality: Measured, meticulous, and protective of the defendant's position.
personas.stance: Argue that the claim is unproven / the charge is unwarranted.

persona_patterns.label: Faithful
persona_patterns.description: Argues that a summary/answer is faithful to its source (summary-evaluation pair).

personas.name: Faithful
personas.background: An evaluator defending that the candidate output is grounded in the source.
personas.personality: Careful, source-anchored, and consistency-seeking.
personas.stance: Argue that the output is faithful and consistent with the source.

persona_patterns.label: Unfaithful
persona_patterns.description: Argues that a summary/answer is unfaithful to its source (summary-evaluation pair).

personas.name: Unfaithful
personas.background: An evaluator hunting for hallucinations and unsupported claims.
personas.personality: Suspicious, detail-oriented, and intolerant of unsupported content.
personas.stance: Argue that the output is unfaithful or contains unsupported content.

personas.name: Proponent
personas.background: An agent that defends the retrieved evidence and the answer it supports.
personas.personality: Confident and grounded in the retrieved passages.
personas.stance: Argue that the retrieved evidence supports the proposed answer.

personas.name: Challenger
personas.background: An agent that questions the retrieval and probes for contradicting evidence.
personas.personality: Inquisitive and willing to reject weakly supported answers.
personas.stance: Argue that the retrieved evidence is insufficient or contradicts the answer.

persona_patterns.label: Gold answer advocate
persona_patterns.description: Argues for the correct answer (gold/distractor pair for QA debates).

personas.name: Gold
personas.background: An agent committed to defending the correct answer with sound reasoning.
personas.personality: Rigorous, precise, and grounded in the question's constraints.
personas.stance: Argue that the correct (gold) option is the right answer.

persona_patterns.label: Distractor advocate
persona_patterns.description: Argues for the strongest incorrect option (gold/distractor pair for QA debates).

personas.name: Distractor
personas.background: An agent that mounts the most convincing case for a plausible wrong option.
personas.personality: Persuasive and good at exploiting ambiguity.
personas.stance: Argue that the strongest distractor option is the right answer.

persona_patterns.label: Six Thinking Hats
persona_patterns.description: Edward de Bono's six thinking modes modelled as six distinct personalities.

personas.name: White Hat
personas.background: The information gatherer focused on data and known facts.
personas.personality: Neutral and objective; reports facts without interpretation.
personas.stance: Contribute only facts, figures, and information gaps.

personas.name: Red Hat
personas.background: The voice of intuition and emotion.
personas.personality: Expresses feelings and hunches without needing to justify them.
personas.stance: Contribute emotional and intuitive reactions to the proposal.

personas.name: Black Hat
personas.background: The cautious critic assessing risks.
personas.personality: Careful and judgemental; identifies difficulties and dangers.
personas.stance: Contribute risks, weaknesses, and reasons something may fail.

personas.name: Yellow Hat
personas.background: The optimist assessing value and benefits.
personas.personality: Positive and constructive; seeks feasibility and upside.
personas.stance: Contribute benefits, value, and reasons something may succeed.

personas.name: Green Hat
personas.background: The creative generator of alternatives.
personas.personality: Inventive and lateral; proposes new ideas and options.
personas.stance: Contribute creative alternatives and novel possibilities.

personas.name: Blue Hat
personas.background: The process manager organising the thinking.
personas.personality: Reflective and organising; directs the discussion.
personas.stance: Contribute structure, summaries, and next-step direction.

persona_patterns.label: Domain expert panel
persona_patterns.description: A set of differentiated domain-expert backgrounds for a cross-disciplinary panel.

personas.name: Software Engineer
personas.background: A senior software engineer with deep systems and architecture experience.
personas.personality: Pragmatic and implementation-focused.
personas.stance: Evaluate from a technical feasibility and engineering-cost perspective.

personas.name: Domain Scientist
personas.background: A subject-matter scientist grounded in the relevant research literature.
personas.personality: Evidence-driven and methodical.
personas.stance: Evaluate from a scientific validity and evidence perspective.

personas.name: Product Strategist
personas.background: A product strategist focused on users, market fit, and outcomes.
personas.personality: User-centric and outcome-oriented.
personas.stance: Evaluate from a user-value and strategic-fit perspective.

personas.name: Ethicist
personas.background: An ethicist assessing fairness, safety, and societal impact.
personas.personality: Principled and risk-aware.
personas.stance: Evaluate from an ethical, fairness, and safety perspective.
